STEP 2 TRUE L0 MEASURED. 51.2 GPU-seconds total = 0.0142 accelerator-hours. Measured on the OpenThoughts3 VAL split, never train, because measuring sparsity on data the adapter was fit to would report memorisation rather than representational sparsity. L0 is the adapter class's own cached_l0, so it is the same quantity the training objective shaped; padding is masked out. RESULT: l1w0.001 (README table claims 1.4) measures whole-model mean 3.3699, median 1.7277. l1w0.003 (README table claims 4.3) measures mean 3.7588, median 1.8528. TABLE VERSUS PROSE, adjudicated as the authority requires: the README table at the registered commit says higher l1_weight gives HIGHER L0, its prose at line 48 says higher l1_weight produces sparser adapters with FEWER active features, and they are mutually exclusive. The measurement does NOT resolve this cleanly and is reported as split rather than forced. Per-layer, 21 of 28 layers show the PROSE direction. The whole-model mean shows the TABLE direction, but only because layers 26 and 27 carry L0 an order of magnitude above every other layer - 23.33/24.39 and 18.40/37.25 - and layer 27 alone differs by about 19 features per token, enough to flip the sign of the mean by itself. Excluding those two layers, the mean reverses to the prose direction, 2.0242 versus 1.6770. ON VALUES neither checkpoint reproduces its published figure and, more importantly, the measured SEPARATION between them is a ratio of about 1.12 by mean and 1.07 by median against the 3.07 the table implies. SUBSTANTIVE CONSEQUENCE reported to the operator: the sparsity-sensitivity arm may have materially less leverage than its registered purpose assumes, since the two checkpoints are nearly equally sparse on this data. This is NOT a Q-3 failure - no L0 threshold is registered anywhere, and inventing one after seeing the measurement would be exactly the move pre-registration forbids. Scope caveat recorded: absolute values are slice-dependent and need not match the authors' Val L0, but the between-checkpoint comparison is apples to apples on identical rows, truncation, code and masking. One transformers 5.x defect fixed in our own code rather than in third-party source: _dead_feature_counters is a plain attribute, so meta-device init never materialises it and the class's own forward raises 'Cannot copy out of meta tensor'; it is restored to the zeros __init__ intended, which changes no weight and does not touch the L0 figure computed earlier in the same block. Also corrected a GPU addressing error: docker --gpus device=N remaps the physical card to index 0 inside the container, so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 addressed nothing; the script asserts device_count()==1 rather than trusting the flag, which is what caught it.
